findings.description: PGAI asked the caller 'Am I speaking with Aria?' despite the caller having already identified himself as Michael Foster, the patient.
findings.expected: PGAI should have used the name the caller already provided (Michael Foster) or asked a relevant verification question, not guessed an unrelated name.

findings.description: PGAI ended the call with 'Goodbye' while the patient's refill request was still unresolved, abandoning the caller without completing the handoff or providing a process.
findings.quote: Hello. You've reached the Pretty Good AI test line. Goodbye.
findings.expected: Per expected_behavior, PGAI should have either processed the refill, explained the correct process (pharmacy/portal/appointment), or taken a message for a callback — not terminated the call mid-request.

findings.description: PGAI broke character by announcing 'You've reached the Pretty Good AI test line' instead of maintaining the Pivot Point Orthopedics receptionist persona.
findings.quote: Hello. You've reached the Pretty Good AI test line. Goodbye.
findings.expected: PGAI should have stayed in character as the clinic receptionist and completed the promised transfer to patient support or otherwise resolved the refill request.

findings.description: PGAI never collected the caller's pharmacy information (Walgreens on Market Street) or medication details before attempting to hand off the refill request.
findings.quote: I'll connect you to our patient support team so they could help with your naproxen refill request.
findings.expected: PGAI should have gathered the pharmacy name/location and confirmed the medication and dosage on file before transferring or taking a message, so the request could actually be actioned.

passed_criteria: Verified caller identity with full name and date of birth before discussing the request
Did not fabricate a refill confirmation — avoided claiming 'I've sent the refill' without a mechanism
Acknowledged inability to locate the record rather than hallucinating prescription details
Offered an alternative (patient support team) when it could not find the record
notes: The call ended abruptly after the transfer attempt with a 'test line' message and hang-up, suggesting a failed handoff flow. The caller's final plea ('Wait, hold on — I still need that refill') received no response. The 'Aria' name guess appears to be a confused identity check, possibly conflating the agent's own name with the caller's.
